In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cation-poor complex metallic alloys (Ba(Eu)-Au-Ga(Al) systems) feature a unique interplay between the chemical composition and the structural and magnetic properties.

the structural and magnetic properties of the complex metallic alloys are determined by the interplay of the following factors: (a) the crystal structure, (b) the chemical composition, (c) the electronic structure, (d) the magnetic properties, (e) the oxidation states of the elements, and (f) the chemical bonding.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cation-poor complex metallic alloys in the Ba(Eu)-M-Au(Al, Ga) systems are characterized by a variety of structural motifs that are controlled by the interplay of electronic and geometrical factors.

the formation of cation-poor complex metallic alloys (CCMA) Ba(Eu)-Al(Ga)-Au systems is controlled by the following factors: (1) the formation of anionic networks with complete site mixing, (2) a successive decrease of the local symmetry, and (3) a maximization of heteroatomic bonds.
the Ba(Eu)-Al(Ga)-Au system provides a unique opportunity to explore the structural and chemical diversity in cation-poor complex metallic alloys.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cation-poor CMA Ba(Eu)-Tr-Au (Tr = Al/Ga) systems feature a variety of crystal structures and atom distributions that can be tuned by the choice of trivalent metal and by varying the composition.
a combination of structural and electronic factors is required to explain the structural and magnetic features of complex metallic alloys.
a high number of cation vacancies in the crystallographic framework of the complex metallic alloys is a prerequisite for the stabilization of cation-poor compounds.
